title: Celigo Alternatives: 7 Integration Platforms Compared
summary: Celigo alternatives span enterprise iPaaS and focused connectors; determine which fits your budget, integration complexity, and feature requirements.
body_markdown:
## Where Activepieces fits as a Celigo alternative


If most of your flow volume doesn't run through the ERP's order-to-cash path, Activepieces fits.


> **The decision turns on one condition: whether most of your flow volume runs through the ERP's order-to-cash path.


It suits general cross-app workflows moving off Celigo, not integration apps built around the ERP, and because **every plan, including free, allows unlimited flows** , adding a process no longer adds a line to the renewal.


### Where it fits and where it does not


If your Celigo flows are mostly alerts, record creation and approvals, you're paying for ERP depth you don't use.


Activepieces connects everyday apps through triggers and actions, drawing on 750 integrations, with an MIT-licensed core you can run on your own infrastructure, so you're not dependent on a third party for uptime.


If the bulk of your volume is order, invoice and fulfilment sync inside the ERP, Activepieces carries less ERP-grade connector depth than Celigo, since roughly 60% of its 750 integrations are community-contributed breadth across everyday apps, and the earlier condition sends you back to Celigo.


You choose the hosting. On the cloud plans,[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) runs the platform. If you self-host the MIT-licensed core, your team patches, upgrades and monitors it, so the licence saving becomes a staffing line.


### Cloud plan pricing


On the cloud plans the prices are flat and monthly.


According to Activepieces, the Free plan costs $0 per month, enough to build the flow below and see whether the tool suits your team before any budget approval, so there's no financial risk to getting started.


The[Plus plan costs $20 per month](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) , or $240 a year. The[Team plan costs $200 per month](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) , or $2,400 a year, ten times Plus, so move up only when the extra capability is something you need rather than something you might.


### Example ERP order exception approval workflow


Short enough for one person to read in a minute: that is what to take from the flow below. It is a complete exception path built only from a trigger, three actions and an error branch.


1. A webhook or new-order trigger starts the flow when an order arrives.
2. A create-record action writes the order into your tracking system.
3. A Slack message tells the owning team the order needs review.
4. An approval step holds the flow until someone signs off.
5. If any step fails, an error branch runs a notify-owner step, so a failure reaches a person instead of sitting in a log.


Look at the diagram's side note, which lists the ERP-specific order-to-cash apps this flow doesn't replicate. That gap is the line between a workflow tool and an ERP integration platform.


If your flows stay on the right side of it, browse the[available pieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces) . Start free.
